AgentMercury: Synthetic Environments for Agentic Evaluation

An Author, Another Author

Abstract

AgentMercury studies synthetic environments for evaluating agentic systems, with checkpoint and rollback support and a multi-agent sandbox.

1. Introduction

We present a benchmark and a world model for tool-use trajectories. Agentic systems increasingly act inside long-horizon environments where a single mistake compounds across many steps, so the ability to checkpoint intermediate state and roll back to a known-good point is central to both training and evaluation. In this work we describe the construction of a synthetic environment generator, the way we seed tasks with verifiable success conditions, and how a multi-agent sandbox records full trajectories for later judging. We compare against prior reward-hacking-prone setups and show that explicit rollback reduces wasted rollouts while improving the reliability and reproducibility of the reported numbers.
